title: Price bands without a UDF
prompt: The starter labels products with a UDF. It works on the sample but stops the job on products that have no price yet, and the team would rather not run Python for this anyway. Rewrite `solve(products)` so it returns `product_id`, `name` and `price_band` by the rules below.
rules: `budget` below 15.00, `standard` from 15.00 up to but not including 50.00, and `premium` from 50.00 up.
A product with a missing `unit_price` is `unpriced`.
Return `product_id`, `name` and `price_band`, all text, in that order. Keep every product.
hints: `F.when(condition, value)` chains: `.when(...).when(...).otherwise(...)`. The first true condition wins.
A comparison with a missing price isn't true, so a missing price falls through to `otherwise`. Give `premium` its own `.when(...)`, so `otherwise` is left for the missing prices.
Check the boundaries: 15.00 is `standard` and 50.00 is `premium`.
